facts.claim: Pretoria was founded in 1855 by Marthinus Pretorius, who named it after his father Andries Pretorius, a Voortrekker leader; he bought the farms Elandspoort and Koedoespoort to create a town for the new Transvaal state.

source.title: Pretoria: The Founding of the City
source.author: South African History Online (no individual author)
source.quote: By end of 1855, the two farms were officially declared as a town.

facts.claim: Pretoria became the capital of the Transvaal in 1860, replacing Potchefstroom.

source.title: Pretoria: The Founding of the City
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: In 1860, Pretoria became the Capital city of Transvaal, superseding Potchefstroom in this role.

facts.claim: Name origin: named after Andries Pretorius (Voortrekker leader) by his son Marthinus. The alternative name Tshwane is explained by SAHO as a Setswana word, with other theories also given.

source.title: Pretoria, now known as Tshwane
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: Founded in 1855 by Marthinus Pretorius, son of Andries Pretorius

facts.claim: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria is the administrative (executive) capital, Cape Town the legislative capital where Parliament sits, Bloemfontein the judicial capital with the Supreme Court of Appeal.

source.title: South Africa's provinces
source.quote: is the judicial capital and home to the Supreme Court of Appeal.

facts.claim: The split came from negotiations between Britain and the defeated Boer republics; the administration was based in Pretoria (capital of the Transvaal), Parliament in Cape Town, the judiciary in Bloemfontein (capital of the Orange Free State). The Constitutional Court now sits in Johannesburg.

source.title: South Africa's Three Capitals
source.author: John Campbell
source.quote: The administration was based in Pretoria

facts.claim: Pretoria achieved official city status on 14 October 1931.

source.title: Pretoria receives city status
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: On 14 October 1931, Pretoria achieved official city status.

timeline.claim: With the Union of South Africa, Pretoria becomes the administrative capital; the Union Buildings (completed 1913) house the administration.

timeline.claim: Under apartheid-era group areas policy, Laudium is set aside as the residential area for Pretoria's Indian population (Group Areas Act of 1950 described as the cornerstone of apartheid).

source.title: Pretoria the Segregated city
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: was set aside as the new residential area for the Indian population of Pretoria

timeline.claim: Nelson Mandela, South Africa's first democratically elected President, is inaugurated at the Union Buildings.

source.title: Union Buildings, Pretoria
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: Inauguration of South Africa's first democratically elected President, Nelson Mandela.

timeline.claim: The South African Geographical Names Council approves the name Tshwane for the city; the change was later rejected by many of Pretoria's citizens and the city is still commonly called Pretoria.

source.title: Pretoria (Tshwane): The Naming of a City
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: This new name was approved on 26 May 2005, by the South African Geographical Names Council (SAGNC)

places.name: Union Buildings
places.what: The seat of South Africa's government on Meintjieskop, overlooking Pretoria, designed by Herbert Baker and completed in 1913. It houses the offices of the President and the terraced gardens hold events including Nelson Mandela's 1994 inauguration.

source.title: Union Buildings, Pretoria
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: Designed and built by Herbert Baker and completed in 1913

source.title: Union Buildings, Pretoria
source.author: South African History Online
source.quote: It is situated on Meintjieskop

facts.label: Site choice
facts.value: Baker rejected the Market Street blocks as unworthy of the capital of united South Africa

source.title: The Birth of the Union Buildings
source.author: Claus Schutte
source.quote: I thought this site unworthy of the capital buildings of the now united South Africa.

facts.label: 1956 women's march
facts.value: About 20,000 women marched to the Union Buildings against apartheid pass laws

source.title: Union Buildings, Pretoria

source.quote: protesting against Apartheid laws, undertook a procession to the Union Buildings

facts.label: Gardens

source.quote: magnificently laid exclusively with indigenous plants

places.name: Ditsong National Museum of Natural History (formerly Transvaal Museum)
places.what: Gauteng's only natural history museum, in central Pretoria. Founded as the state museum of the old Transvaal republic in 1892, it holds hominid fossils and the specimen known as Mrs Ples.

facts.label: Founded
facts.value: 1 December 1892 as the Staatsmuseum of the ZAR

source.title: Ditsong: National Museum of Natural History
source.quote: founded as the Staatsmuseum of the ZAR on the 1st of December 1892

facts.label: Gauteng status
facts.value: Only natural history museum in Gauteng

source.title: Ditsong: National Museum of Natural History
source.quote: the only natural history museum in Gauteng

facts.label: Collections
facts.value: Hominid fossils from the Cradle of Humankind

source.title: Ditsong: National Museum of Natural History
source.quote: hominid fossils from the Cradle of Humankind World Heritage Site and associated fauna

places.name: Rietvlei Nature Reserve
places.what: A nature reserve built around a dam, a short distance from Pretoria in the Tshwane municipality. It protects grassland and wildlife.

source.title: Rietvlei Nature Reserve - a land of water
source.quote: A stone's throw away from South Africa's capital, the city of Pretoria in Tshwane Municipality.

source.title: Rietvlei Nature Reserve - a land of water
source.quote: Home to the endangered Bankenveld grassland and around 2000 different animals.

facts.label: History
facts.value: Dam dug in the 1930s; reserve proclaimed and opened 1948

source.title: Rietvlei Nature Reserve - a land of water
source.quote: the nature reserve was only created, proclaimed and opened to the public in 1948.

places.name: Freedom Park
places.what: A heritage precinct of memorial sites on Salvokop Hill, Pretoria, commemorating those who died in conflicts that shaped South Africa. It includes S'khumbuto, a wall of names and a gallery of leaders.

source.title: Freedom Park, Pretoria: monument to South Africa's liberation struggle in Gauteng
source.quote: a multifaceted heritage precinct that consists of a series of memorial sites

facts.label: Reeds
facts.value: Semicircle of 200 reeds signifying rebirth as a nation

source.title: Freedom Park, Pretoria: monument to South Africa's liberation struggle in Gauteng
source.quote: a semicircle of 200 reeds

source.title: FREEDOM PARK
source.author: Ndivhuwo Khangale
source.quote: This heritage site on the Salvokop hill in Pretoria.

myth.claim: Pretoria is South Africa's only capital.
myth.truth: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (administrative/executive), Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial).

source.title: South Africa's provinces
source.quote: is the legislative capital and is where the country's Parliament is found.
